Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "could you make a weekday watering rota for one normal week at our greenhouse, just monday to friday, no weekend shifts. the people available are Mina, Joel and Priya, and please spread the days around as evenly as possible, with nobody assigned more than two days. One person should be responsible each day, and they need to check both the east bench and west bench moisture sensors at 7:00 in the morning before watering. Each bench has its own reading, so decide what to do separately for the two benches, not as one combined reading. if a bench's reading is below 30%, water that bench for 6 minutes. if its reading is 30% or higher, do not water that bench. That second case matters too, please show it clearly so staff don't think they should water every bench every day. Can you set this up as a simple table with the weekday, assigned person, and a clear conditional instruction for each bench? don't fill in any sensor readings or guess which bench will need water; the rota should explain what the assigned person does once they see the readings. Add a short note that checks happen at 7:00 before any watering, and keep the instructions easy to scan while someone is working.", "output": "Create a simple weekday watering rota for one normal week at our greenhouse. Include Monday through Friday only, with no weekend shifts. Assign one person each day from Mina, Joel, and Priya, spreading the five assignments as evenly as possible and assigning no one more than two days.

The assigned person must check the separate moisture sensors for the east bench and west bench at 7:00 in the morning, before watering. For each bench independently:
- If its reading is below 30%, water that bench for 6 minutes.
- If its reading is 30% or higher, do not water that bench.

Present the rota in an easy-to-scan table with the weekday, assigned person, and a clear conditional instruction for each bench. Do not fill in sensor readings or guess which benches will need water; explain what the assigned person should do after seeing each reading. Add a short note that the checks happen at 7:00 before any watering."}]
